title: Why Your Vote Counts Down the Ballot, Not Just at the Top : California 2026
description:
The loudest races aren’t always the closest. In California, the races down the ballot can come down to a few votes, and independent voters are big enough to decide them.

More than 1 in 5 California voters has no party. That gives them the power to decide offices the headlines ignore, like Insurance Commissioner, the office that regulates your insurance rates.

You don’t need to belong to a party to vote in these races. You just need to vote the whole ballot.

See the 15 races where the independent vote can decide the outcome:
https://ivn.us/15-races-where-democratic-socialists-can-reshape-california-politics/

About IVN
Independent Voter News (IVN.us) is a nonpartisan news platform. It covers elections from the voter’s perspective, not a party’s, with data-driven reporting and verifiable sources. IVN does not endorse candidates or parties. The goal is to give voters the information they need to decide for themselves.

Election Day: Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
Learn more at IVN.us
